description: Single en catalog whose translations carry every StringInterpolator escape sequence and every index-advancement boundary of the escape state machine. Every key here RESOLVES, so DefaultStrings.interpolateTemplate runs interpolateStrictly - this is the strict half of the plan v7 section 8.3 interpolation-escape clause. Every translation is deliberately strict-VALID because LocalizedStringLoader.validatePlaceholderReferences (LocalizedStringLoader.java:2308) runs the same strict scan at load time; a strict-invalid translation raises LocalizedStringLoadingException and aborts the whole corpus build rather than producing a case row (re-verified in this review with throwaway probe fixtures). The last two keys add generated language-form placeholders: one whose form translation itself contains an escape (single-pass expansion), and one whose only reference sits inside an escaped region (never expanded at all).

en.esc.backslash.tripled-before-placeholder: \\\{{name}} is a backslash then a literal placeholder
en.esc.mixed.all-forms: Literal \{{count}} vs real {{count}}, close \}} and backslash \\ end

esc.generated.single-pass.commentary: The language-form translations contain an escaped placeholder that must survive expansion without being re-interpolated against the outer context.

esc.generated.escaped-only-reference.commentary: The sole reference to the declared generated placeholder sits inside an escaped region, so placeholderNamesIn never reports it and it is never expanded.
